fact: The Ministry of Digital Transition presented digital-training infrastructure investments in the PND 2026-2030, with an estimated budget of 95 billion FCFA, aiming to train tens of thousands of digital talents across the territory, under a strategy pillar on developing digital skills.
Cote d'Ivoire's digital minister and ITU discussed efforts to expand digital skills programmes for workforce development and digital inclusion.

The Conseil des ministres communique of 4 February 2026 says the IDA-financed PADCI phase 1 loan, concluded 17 October 2025, provides for developing advanced and intermediate digital skills, targeting young people and women in particular (US$5m component per the appraisal document).
CIPESA says ANSUT's universal access efforts include digital literacy and skills programs.

The Ministry of Digital Transition's draft 2025 budget lists developing digital skills for women, young people and vulnerable people among its activities, as part of the digital support project funded at FCFA 1.5 billion.

fact: A youth ministry adviser said that since 2023 the 21 ministries in the government's Programme jeunesse du gouvernement (PJGouv) had given digital skills to 51,601 young people, 6,400 of them through Trace Academia and Africa Digital Academy courses.

The Prime Minister launched the GENIE project on 26 February 2025, under which 35 DigiGreen centres in schools, universities and town halls in Abidjan and Grand-Bassam are to train over 45,000 young people in digital skills, co-financed at 5.5 billion FCFA by the government, KOICA and GGGI.

Minister Djibril Ouattara stated the aim of training 200,000 learners in Cote d'Ivoire in cybersecurity, networking and AI skills by 2030 under the Africa Digital Power programme of the TIA Foundation and Cisco.

Cisco, Cybastion and the Ivorian government's Africa DigiEmpower programme aims to train 200,000 young people and women across 10 regions in cybersecurity, networking and AI by 2030, building on two summers of training at U.S. Embassy American Spaces.

GGGI says it launched the USD 8.25 million GENIE project with KOICA in partnership with the Government of Côte d'Ivoire on 26 February 2025, to set up 35 centres training over 45,000 people in digital literacy and ICT skills, with centres still being set up and about ten to open by mid-2025.
